findings.title: read_api scope for read access to accessible projects
findings.detail: read_api grants read access to the API, including all groups and projects. It does not grant write access, so it covers listing issue titles without create, update or delete rights.
findings.appliesWhen: The app calls project issue list endpoints as the connected person.

steps.detail: Create a user-owned OAuth application in the GitLab account of the developer who will test. Enter a name and redirect URI, select read_api scope, then save. Record the Application ID and Client Secret.
steps.doneWhen: The application shows an Application ID and a Client Secret, with read_api selected and the redirect URI saved.

evidence.quote: Enter a Name and Redirect URI .
Select OAuth 2 Scopes as defined in Authorized Applications .
The OAuth 2 Client ID in the Application ID field.

fields: Redirect URI: the URL where users are sent after authorization
Scope: read_api

steps.title: Redirect the connected person to the GitLab authorization page
steps.detail: Use PKCE as the single documented client type for this flow. Before redirecting, generate a random STATE and a CODE_VERIFIER of 43-128 characters from A-Z, a-z, 0-9, -, ., _, ~, then derive CODE_CHALLENGE as the URL-safe base64 of the binary SHA256 of CODE_VERIFIER without padding. Send the connected person to the /oauth/authorize endpoint with client_id, redirect_uri, response_type=code, state, scope=read_api, code_challenge and code_challenge_method=S256. Do not send client_secret on this flow. The person approves the request and is redirected back with code and the same state value.
steps.doneWhen: The redirect URL contains a code parameter and a state value equal to the generated STATE.

evidence.quote: https://gitlab.example.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=APP_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&state=STATE&scope=REQUESTED_SCOPES&code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE&code_challenge_method=S256&root_namespace_id=ROOT_NAMESPACE_ID This page asks
Before starting the flow, generate the STATE , the CODE_VERIFIER and the CODE_CHALLENGE .
The redirect includes the authorization code , for example:

fields: APP_ID: Application ID from the registered user-owned application (placeholder; user supplies)
REDIRECT_URI: redirect URI saved at registration (placeholder; user supplies)
STATE: unpredictable value generated by the client before the request
CODE_VERIFIER: random 43-128 character string generated by the client and kept secret
CODE_CHALLENGE: URL-safe base64 of SHA256(CODE_VERIFIER), derived by the client
scope: read_api only, no write scopes

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: Exchange the returned code with the PKCE flow only, so no client_secret is sent. POST to the token endpoint with client_id, code, grant_type=authorization_code, redirect_uri and code_verifier set to the same CODE_VERIFIER used to derive CODE_CHALLENGE. Store access_token and refresh_token from the response. The token is then used as a Bearer token for read-only issue listing.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains access_token, token_type bearer, expires_in and refresh_token.
